test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The second five year plan of India was completed in ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1961**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** of India was functional during the period from **1956 to 1961**. It officially concluded on **March 31, 1961**.
 
• This plan was based on the **P.C. Mahalanobis Model**, which prioritized **rapid industrialization** and the development of **heavy and basic industries**.
 
• The primary aim was to achieve a **socialistic pattern of society**, a goal adopted during the **Avadi Session** of the **Indian National Congress** in **1955**.
 
• It focused heavily on the **public sector** to drive the national economy, following the guidelines of the **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956**.
 
• The plan saw the establishment of major **hydroelectric power projects** and five **steel plants** at **Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela** with foreign collaboration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956):**

 
 
• It was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model** and focused mainly on **agriculture, price stability, and power**.
 
• It was a successful plan as it achieved a growth rate of **3.6%**, exceeding the target of **2.1%**.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966):**
 
 
• This plan followed the completion of the second plan in **1961**. It aimed to make India a **self-reliant** and **self-generating economy**.
 
• However, due to the **Sino-Indian War (1962)** and the **Indo-Pakistani War (1965)**, the plan failed to meet its targets.
 
 
 
• **Plan Holidays (1966–1969):**
 
 
• Due to the failure of the Third Plan and the devaluation of the **Indian Rupee**, the government declared **Plan Holidays**.
 
• During this period, three **annual plans** were implemented instead of a comprehensive five-year strategy.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969–1974):**
 
 
• Launched under the leadership of **Indira Gandhi**, it focused on **growth with stability** and the 14 major **Indian banks were nationalized** in **1969**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Planning Commission** was the nodal agency responsible for drafting the Five-Year Plans. It was established on **March 15, 1950**.
 
• The **National Development Council (NDC)** was responsible for the final approval of these plans to ensure the participation of **State Governments**.
 
• In **January 2015**, the **NDA government** replaced the Planning Commission with the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India).
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** is often referred to as the **"Industrial and Transport Plan"** because nearly **28%** of the total outlay was dedicated to **transport and communications**, and **20%** to **industry and mining**.
 
• The targeted growth rate for the Second Plan was **4.5%**, but the actual growth achieved was approximately **4.27%**.
